slides.headline: He designed the microprocessor architecture that still shapes chips inside billions of devices today.
Vinod Dham
slides.body: Born in Pune, Dham studied electrical engineering in Delhi before moving to the US in the 1970s. He joined Intel and became one of the lead architects behind the Pentium processor - the chip that powered the personal computer boom of the 1990s.

slides.headline: Millions of PCs ran on a chip he helped design.
slides.body: Dham led the Pentium's development team through the 1990s, earning him the nickname "Father of the Pentium chip" in industry circles. The architecture decisions from that era still echo in how modern processors are built.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: India's growth story runs through its diaspora too.
slides.body: Decades before India had its own chip design ecosystem, Indian engineers abroad were already shaping the hardware the entire world runs on. That same talent pool is now a reason global semiconductor firms are opening design centers back in India.
